dimensions.title: SCA dependency-declaration pack against its 1000 target
dimensions.detail: 1000 of 1000 rules are authored (target reached 2026-10-25; the pack is frozen at 1000). The owner approved drobon.pack.sca/v1 on 2026-10-25 and directed the pack to the 1000 target. Each rule classifies declared dependency text in one ecosystem and one artifact, carries 2 positives and 2 negatives that the validator executes, and has its own pattern, record and remediation entry. A rule never states that a version is affected by an advisory, so this pack does not depend on the GHSA/OSV/NVD data lock.
dimensions.nextAction: Keep the pack frozen at 1000: additive growth is closed, and any replacement stays an owner decision. The open work is App-side (an SCA pack loader); the independent evaluation pairs already ship with every rule (`eval.sca`).

dimensions.title: Independent evaluation cases for SCA rules
dimensions.unit: rules with an independent eval case
dimensions.detail: 1000 of 1000 SCA rules carry an independent evaluation case: one positive fixture and one negative control per rule, both authored for the case (mode `sca-document`) and disjoint from the rule's own declared validator tests. The runner parses each fixture and evaluates the rule's predicate against it, so a case can fail; none does (0 FN, 0 FP on the SCA cohort). This measures the authored population, not real-world effectiveness.
dimensions.nextAction: Keep the invariant: a new SCA rule ships with its independent positive case and negative control in the same batch.

dimensions.title: Independent evaluation: rules with a positive case
dimensions.detail: 3135 of 3135 rules carry an independent positive case. BLK-EVAL-01 was closed on 2026-10-25 by the owner's instruction to finish the remaining evaluation work, choosing the recorded option (a): a case may declare evidence shorter than 4 characters only when it sets `shortEvidence: true`, and the runner then requires that text to equal the detector's COMPLETE match — a 2–3 character fragment of a longer match is still a false negative (regression-tested in scripts/test-eval.mjs). The eight SAST marker rules (416, 417, 418, 423, 424, 678, 692, 731) carry their positives under that rule.
dimensions.nextAction: Keep the invariant: a new rule ships with its own positive case (and `shortEvidence` only where the whole match is shorter than four characters).

dimensions.title: Independent evaluation: rules with a negative control
dimensions.detail: 3135 of 3135 rules carry a negative control: an authored fixture on which the rule must stay silent (ordinary, idiomatic code/config per language; a plain status response per DAST body surface; one control per SCA rule). Fixtures are authored for the case and never derived from the rule's own declared test, which would be circular (counting rule in scripts/eval-coverage-report.mjs).
dimensions.nextAction: Keep the invariant: a new rule ships with its own positive case and a control.

dimensions.title: Universal rules with both a positive case and a negative control
dimensions.detail: Universal rules run on every analysed file, so they carry the highest false-positive cost. All 11 now have an independent positive case and an independent negative control.

dimensions.title: DAST rules evaluable through the App response surface

Body rules are reachable but bounded by the clip.
